item.title: Mochi Diffusion enables native Stable Diffusion and FLUX.2 on Mac
item.description:
Mochi Diffusion enables native Stable Diffusion and FLUX.2 on Mac

Mochi Diffusion is a new native macOS application that allows users to run Stable Diffusion and FLUX.2 Klein models locally and completely offline. The app is built with SwiftUI and leverages Apple’s Core ML implementation for Stable Diffusion and the Iris pipeline for FLUX.2 Klein and Z-Image Turbo to achieve maximum performance and speed with reduced memory requirements.

🧩 How it works

The application supports multiple model pipelines and compute configurations:

  • Core ML Stable Diffusion: Uses specially converted models for Apple hardware. These are extremely fast and memory efficient, especially on Apple Silicon Macs with Neural Engine, though each model generates images of a fixed size baked in during conversion.
  • FLUX.2 Klein and Z-Image Turbo: Run via the Iris pipeline with native Metal GPU acceleration. No conversion is required for FLUX.2 Klein models.
  • Draw Things Server: Mochi Diffusion can also generate images using models hosted on a Draw Things server.

For Stable Diffusion, users must convert or download Core ML models. The split_einsum version is compatible with all compute unit options, including the Neural Engine, while the original version is only compatible with the CPU & GPU option. Users need to select the correct model version corresponding to their chosen compute option.

⚙️ Key details

  • Compute Options: CPU & Neural Engine provides a balance between speed and low memory usage. CPU & GPU may be faster on M1 Max, Ultra, and later chips but uses more memory.
  • Model Management: The model folder is created by default under the user’s home directory, customizable in Settings. Users create a new folder with the desired display name and move or extract converted models into it.
  • Compilation Time: The first use of a model may take up to 2 minutes for the Neural Engine to compile a cached version; subsequent generations are much faster.
  • Input Handling: FLUX.2 Klein supports up to 4 input images. Due to pipeline constraints, Mochi automatically resizes inputs to fit the attention budget and indicates the new sizes in the UI.
  • Features: Includes a built-in gallery with import, save, and sync support. Generated images are saved as PNG with embedded generation settings, readable by AUTOMATIC1111-compatible tools and Civitai uploads (viewable in Finder’s Get Info window).
  • Capabilities: Supports generating images based on a starting image or using ControlNet with Stable Diffusion.

🚀 Availability

The app is available for macOS. Users can obtain FLUX.2 Klein model components (text_encoder, tokenizer, transformer, and vae) from provided download links or using the download_model.sh script.

#MochiDiffusion #StableDiffusion #MacOS #CoreML #FLUX2 #ImageGeneration

Source: MochiDiffusion/MochiDiffusion

item.title: New Tag Autocomplete Extension for Stable Diffusion AUTOMATIC1111 Web UI
item.description:
New Tag Autocomplete Extension for Stable Diffusion AUTOMATIC1111 Web UI

Tag Autocomplete is an extension for the popular AUTOMATIC1111 web UI for Stable Diffusion that provides suggested tags from image booru boards. It displays autocompletion hints for recognized tags to improve prompt accuracy.

🔍 Overview

The extension displays autocompletion hints for recognized tags from image booru boards such as Danbooru and e621. These tags are primarily used for browsing Anime-style illustrations, but they are relevant to a wide range of Stable Diffusion models.

Feature Description
Danbooru & e621 Tags Top 100k tags by post count as of November 2022
Wildcard Support Works with wildcard files from extensions or scripts
Extra Networks Support for Extra Network previews
UI Modes Dark and Light mode support with specific tag colors

🧩 How it works

Completion is triggered by typing a double underscore (__). The extension searches for wildcard files in every extension folder and the scripts/wildcards folder to support legacy versions. It also supports nested folders for grouped wildcards. Because this was one of the first extensions available, it appears high in the inbuilt extensions list when sorting by “oldest first.”

⚙️ Key details

Users can locate the extension by using CTRL + F to search for text on the extensions page. It is compatible with wildcard files used by the AUTOMATIC1111 wildcards extension and other similar scripts. Completion provides exact tags that match training data for many popular models.

🚀 Availability

Installation is available through three primary methods:

  • Using the inbuilt available extensions list within the web UI.
  • Manual cloning of the extension files from the repository.
  • Downloading pre-packaged versions from the project’s Releases page.

💡 Why it matters

Most custom Stable Diffusion models were trained using booru tag information or merged with models that were. Using exact tags in prompts can improve composition and consistency, even if the model itself is designed for a photorealistic style.

#StableDiffusion #Danbooru #AUTOMATIC1111 #AItools #ImageGeneration

Source: DominikDoom/a1111-sd-webui-tagcomplete

item.title: Suno Launches Visuals Feature for AI Music Video Generation
item.description:
Suno Launches Visuals Feature for AI Music Video Generation

Suno has introduced image and video generation capabilities in its latest effort to expand beyond its role as an AI music platform. The new feature, named “Visuals,” allows users to transform Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or create images via prompt descriptions that can serve as thumbnails and album artwork.

🧩 How it works

The Visuals feature generates images and 15-second videos that automatically sync with Suno songs. From the interface, users can select which section of the track to use, up to a maximum of 15 seconds, and select a reference image to build the generated video clip.

There are three options available for the starting image reference:

  • Selecting one of the original character presets provided by Suno.
  • Uploading a user’s own photo or artwork.
  • Generating the image directly on Suno using descriptive prompts.

For video generation, users can select whether the reference image is used as the start or end frame, making it easier to edit the 15-second clips together. There is a toggle to automatically lipsync vocals to the generated video, along with tools for adjusting aspect ratio and clip length. The image generation capabilities also allow users to select specific aspect ratios, optimizing results for landscape or portrait modes and online platforms.

⚙️ Key details

Visuals includes a dedicated video editing timeline for assembling clips into longer videos and adding customizable song lyric text. The H3 Move AI model, based on H3 from MiniMax, powers this feature.

Suno states that the AI has been “optimized for our community including adding additional protections and safeguards,” which include a “suite of new text and visual filters” designed to block the use or generation of the likeness of specific artists, public figures, copyrighted works, and IP.

The feature uses its own “Visuals credits” to generate videos and images. These credits are distinct from the song credits used to make AI music, meaning users will have additional expenses to pay in order to use this new feature.

🚀 Availability

Visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android platforms. The exact layout differs across Suno’s desktop and mobile interfaces, but users will find a new Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. Web users can also access Visuals by selecting the three-dot menu on a song in their library.

💡 Context and reception

The launch of Visuals follows Suno introducing a Speech feature in October for generating spoken words and voiceovers. In the YouTube video for the Visuals launch, one user commented “FIX AUDIO BEFORE ADDING CRAP NOBODY ASKED FOR,” a sentiment that other commenters are echoing.

#Suno #AImusic #AImusicvideos #Imagegeneration

Source: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music

item.title: BFL Releases FLUX 3, Training Models on Video Signals Together
item.description:
BFL Releases FLUX 3, Training Models on Video Signals Together

Intro

BFL released FLUX 3, training a new image generation model on video signals together to improve temporal consistency and understanding of motion.

🧩 Origins

Stable Diffusion’s release prompted Dustin Podell and others to go fulltime into AI. Podell stuck to human content creation while immersing in AI content creation with Andreas Blattmann and Stability AI’s image generation team. After Stability AI fell apart, Anj Midha helped the core group spin out to BFL, which built the FLUX series.

🔍 FLUX 3’s Approach

BFL’s argument for training FLUX 3 was to combine three signals: a still shows where the ball is, a video shows how it got there, and the sound of impact can tell when it hit something even if the camera missed contact. A key example in the FLUX 3 release is the horse in motion.

⚙️ Video Upscaling

FLUX 3 derives its video upscaler from the same FLUX 3 backbone. Sharpening each frame independently might look terrific, but playing it back can show shimmering as the upscaler makes slightly different decisions per frame. Temporal consistency matters even for higher-resolution files. Andreas Blattmann notes that ordinary 2D video contains evidence about what objects look like from other angles.

🚀 Technical Execution

An autoregressive model can learn from all tokens in a training example at once. On the diffusion side, the team distilled long sampling processes down to a handful of steps. Dustin Podell’s early Kontext experiment showed that a model able to draw a dog wearing a hat seemed to know where hats go. A few hours of training got the model to place a logo on a shirt, which was rough but sufficient for offsite discussion. The team then spent months refining the data and model.

💡 Unexpected Use Case

Users fed FLUX old, degraded family photos to restore them, then shared the pictures with families. Podell hadn’t predicted this use. After discussing identity preservation across edits and frames, he noted it’s a nice example of users noticing when something is done right.

#StableDiffusion #AI #FLUX3 #VideoGeneration #ImageGeneration

Source: Building Visual Intelligence — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs — Latent Space

item.title: ChatGPT gains native GIF creation with Images 2.6 update
item.description:
ChatGPT gains native GIF creation with Images 2.6 update

OpenAI has rolled out an update to ChatGPT that adds native animated GIF generation.

🔍 Overview

  • ChatGPT can now create GIFs from a text prompt or an uploaded photo.
  • The capability is part of the new Images 2.6 model.
  • Before this update, ChatGPT could not generate GIFs in a single step.

🧩 How it works

  • Users provide a prompt such as “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” or upload an image.
  • The model returns an animated GIF and also offers controls to:
    • Adjust the animation speed.
    • Edit individual frames.
    • View the GIF frame by frame.
    • Share the result.

⚙️ Key details

  • Images 2.6 also speeds up regular image generation.
  • OpenAI reports that users now generate over 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT and its API, up from 3 billion in September.
  • New API variants introduced with the rollout:
Model Variant Capability
Images 2.6 Native GIF creation and faster image generation
GPT‑Image‑2.6 Flare Faster image generation
GPT‑Image‑2.6 Sunburst Higher‑quality image generation

🚀 Availability

  • Images 2.6 is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop, and mobile apps.

💡 Why it matters

  • The update turns GIF creation into a native, single‑step operation within ChatGPT, expanding the range of media users can produce directly from text.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #GIF #ImageGeneration

Source: ChatGPT will now make you animated GIFs

item.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5
item.description:
OpenAI introduces ChatGPT Images 2.5

OpenAI has released ChatGPT Images 2.5, an update to image generation models that have been used for more than 3 billion images across ChatGPT Images and the GPT‑Image models in the API.

⚙️ Key details

This latest release includes several improvements:

  • Faster response times
  • Better ability to preserve subjects in reference photos
  • Improved instruction-following ability across multiple turns

🚀 Availability

Two new model IDs are available in the API:

Model ID Use Case
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst Workflows where editing precision matters most
gpt-image-2.5-flare Fast, high-quality everyday image generation

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #ImageGeneration #API

Source: Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5

item.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Sketch Feature
item.description:
OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Images 2.5 and Sketch Feature

OpenAI announced ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Tuesday, introducing updated image generation tools and a new feature called Sketch that allows users to use doodles as part of their prompts.

🧩 How it works

Users can now influence image generation through drawing and direct feedback:

  • Sketch: By typing @Sketch into the chat box, a window appears where users can draw a doodle and then tell ChatGPT how to make an image based on that sketch.
  • Direct Comments: Users can leave comments directly on specific parts of images to request changes, such as changing a cat’s eyes from blue to green.

⚙️ Key details

OpenAI stated that ChatGPT Images 2.5 provides several improvements over Images 2.0:

Feature Improvement
Visual Quality More natural lighting and richer textures
Instruction Following Better at following editing instructions across multiple turns
Performance Latency reduced by up to 50% compared with Images 2.0

🚀 Availability

ChatGPT Images 2.5 is currently available for the following users on desktop, mobile, and web:

  • ChatGPT users
  • ChatGPT Work users
  • Codex users

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #AIimages #ImageGeneration

Source: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images

item.title: AI‑Generated Food Images Produce Uncanny, Incoherent Visuals
item.description:
AI‑Generated Food Images Produce Uncanny, Incoherent Visuals

🔍 Overview

“There is a torrent of unappetizing slop coming from restaurants, cafes, and brands that are increasingly turning to AI to generate images promoting their food.”

🧩 How Diffusion Models Work

“Put simply, diffusion models start with an image of pure noise — something like a screenful of static — and gradually remove noise little by little in order to create the requested visual.” “This means that initially coarse structures are recovered first with fine texture details” — Chris Russell, University of Oxford.

⚠️ Why the Images Look Wrong

  • The model can get the basic structure wrong early, then “lump vivid texture details on top of that structure.” (Russell)
  • “This is the same kind of failure as you see when a person is generated with six fingers instead of five.” (Russell)
  • “Diffusion models are notoriously weak at generating thin, continuous, terminating structures.” (Califano)
  • “Noodles, strands, and tendrils are exactly the kind of geometry that trips this up, so you get spaghetti‑like artifacts bleeding into places with no anatomical or culinary logic.” (Califano)
  • Repeating textures such as bubbles and seeds often spill into areas they should not be in. (Califano)
  • “AI image generation reproduces looks without proper knowledge about the world,” (Roland Meyer, University of Zurich).
  • “It doesn’t help that AI has no idea what a sandwich actually is. It has no understanding of the objects it’s creating or the physical world they inhabit.”
  • Food photography is highly stylized with sharp contrasts, intense colors, glossy lighting, and exaggerated shapes, which AI imitates without the professional aesthetic strategies behind them. (Meyer)
  • “These textures might look totally normal if used in an architectural context,” (Cook) “but they become wrong when we imagine it as edible food.”

🍴 Examples of AI‑Generated Food Failures

  • “donut shrimp”
  • “Reubens from the deep”
  • “wormlike noodles”
  • “noodle‑like pastries”
  • “stringy chicken”
  • “construction material masquerading as ice cream”
  • “ice cream masquerading as brains”
  • “monstrous attempt of a burger”
  • “trypophobic burrito from hell, grubs and all”

💡 Implications

  • The lack of world knowledge leads to objects that look plausible but defy culinary logic.
  • Training data and content associations are largely unknown, making it hard to predict or correct these failures. (Cook)
  • The mismatch between AI’s visual imitation and actual food aesthetics raises concerns for brands that rely on AI‑generated marketing imagery.

#AI #food #diffusionmodels #imagegeneration

Source: Why AI food looks like that
